newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Market quiet, prices weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Market quiet, prices weak.

text.p: Millfeed prices were mixed on Friday, weighed down by a lack of buying interest because of ample pastures for grazing in the U.S. Midwest but supported by shorter flour mill times in several areas, dealers said.

"Everything (livestock) is being turned out to pasture throughout the Midwest," one Kansas dealer said. "That would bite into millfeed demand." He said the recent runup in corn prices did not affect midds right now.
One North Carolina dealer noted that flour mills were not running at capacity in his area. "It's five to 5-1/2 days and that's it," he said.
The tone of the market was heavy, a St Louis dealer said. "The nearby does not feel good at all."
Demand for millfeeds for catfish production in the south eased due to cool and wet weather in Mississippi.

"Mississippi needs warm weather and clear skies. People are presuming that when the warm weather comes, the catfish will start eating and things will be good. But as long as it stays cool and wet, demand was expected to be weak," he said.
A Minneapolis dealer said buying interest has waned.
"We are getting warmer. and some flour mills are running up again and produce more feed than we really need," he said.
